priorities.name: Private space for confidential conversations and calls
priorities.issue: Associates routinely can't find a private room for confidential conversations because booths and phone rooms are all in use, and call noise carries across the floor.
whatItLooksLike: There are times when I need to have a confidential conversation, but I cannot find a private location because all available phone rooms and booths are in use.
Lack of white noise to drown out others that work on the phone.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (76/100).
Privacy & Confidentiality: 57 comments, 65% negative; Noise & Distraction: 47 comments, 62% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Assess booth/phone-room capacity and booking against peak demand; test occupancy indicators and time limits before adding enclosed space.
priorities.siteMustDo: Track booth/phone-room demand-vs-availability for two weeks and escalate a sized capacity gap to Workplace Solutions.

priorities.name: Desk reservation clarity and workstation setup
priorities.issue: Associates can't see when a reserved room/desk will free up, and workstations are often left disassembled, costing setup time.
whatItLooksLike: Other associates being in a room that I have reserved for a meeting and me being unable to see when they are scheduled to be out of that capsule room, if they intend to leave at all.
Many times the workspace has been disassembled and requires that I figure out how to reconnect all pieces (monitors, keyboard, mouse). It's not as easy as just plugging in my laptop.

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations: 77 comments, 48% negative (highest-volume theme).

priorities.proposedAction: Review room/desk booking visibility (when a space frees up) and set a standard for how a workstation should be left.
priorities.siteMustDo: Confirm whether the booking tool surfaces end-times; test a 'leave it as you found it' workstation standard.

priorities.name: Workstation hardware reliability
priorities.issue: Reconnecting monitors/keyboard/mouse at shared desks is not plug-and-play, and connectivity is a frequent, highly negative complaint.
whatItLooksLike: Many times the workspace has been disassembled and requires that I figure out how to reconnect all pieces (monitors, keyboard, mouse). It's not as easy as just plugging in my laptop.

evidence.text: Hardware: 64 comments, 52% negative. Connectivity: 31 comments, 65% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Standardize the dock/monitor setup and run routine equipment checks; validate connectivity in weak spots and route to Technology.
priorities.siteMustDo: Inspect workstations, standardize the setup, and log connectivity dead spots for Technology.

protectWhatIsWorking.evidence: 88% positive across 24 comments — the cleaning staff are singled out
